title: Ink Slab Riot — Screen-Printed Festival Stack
description: A gig-poster slide built from stacked all-caps display type squeezed edge-to-edge, pairing a heavy slab face against a condensed sans with a halftone ink-bleed overlay — closer to a letterpress broadside than a standard promo deck.
philosophy: This design refuses polish and the comfort of whitespace. It exists for the raw energy of live music — where the lineup IS the visual, and every square centimetre should feel pulled from a letterpress shop or a Risograph drum. Hierarchy is earned through scale alone, and texture is meaning rather than decoration. It assumes a dark room and an audience that came to feel something, not to read bullet points.
goodFor: Music festival and concert promotional slides
3–4 line artist lineup reveals projected on a dark stage screen
Single-date event announcements with a venue ticker callout
Brand decks for independent music venues or record labels
avoidFor: Slides requiring more than two levels of body-text hierarchy
Corporate SaaS or fintech product launches
Academic presentations with citations or dense paragraph prose
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Feels like a freshly pulled letterpress broadside — urgent, physical, slightly imperfect. Type dominates every corner with no breathing room; hierarchy is carved purely through scale contrast between a massive headline and a tight secondary band. A coarse halftone grain bleeds edge-to-edge like over-inked Risograph drum passes, texturing the darkness with analog noise. Avoid digital cleanliness, centered symmetry, or any decorative illustration — the type IS the image.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed, zero-margin canvas — type runs wall-to-wall with no padding relief. A 12-column grid where the headline stack spans all 12 columns across two to three staggered rows, alternating flush-left and flush-right to build tension. A halftone texture layer bleeds past all four edges at reduced opacity over the entire background. A sub-label — date or venue ticker — anchors hard to the bottom edge, separated from the main stack by a single rule line.

examples.promptCore: Raw, confrontational energy of a hand-pulled screen-print: every line of type fights for dominance through sheer scale alone, nothing softened by margin or air. Compositional rhythm is dense and vertical — stacked rows lock together like wood type on a press bed, the compression itself carrying the excitement. Halftone grain bleeds through the background and into the lighter type bands, softening edges just enough to feel analogue and imperfect rather than rendered. Avoid spatial generosity, decorative flourish, or centred symmetry; this must feel printed and pulled, never designed.

examples.layoutNotes: Type bleeds edge-to-edge on a 12-column grid with only a tight ~3% horizontal inset — letterforms nearly graze the frame on all sides. Content is three to four stacked artist-name rows filling roughly 85% of vertical height, alternating between a massive display-slab band and a compressed condensed-sans band, with hierarchy earned through scale contrast alone. A full-bleed horizontal rule anchors a venue-and-date ticker strip flush to the bottom edge, spanning the entire width. No top header band, no slide number; a halftone texture layer sits above the background fill but beneath all type.
